text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Tuesday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- President Guntis Ulmanis has called on Economy Minister Guntars Krasts to form a new government.

- Newspapers publish the possible list of ministers in the new government: Deputy Prime Minister Juris Kaksitis, Foreign Minister Valdis Birkavs, Minister of Interior Ziedonis Chevers, Minister of Economics Andris Ameriks, Minister of Transport Vilis Krishtopans, Minister of Agriculture Roberts Dilba, Minister of Education and Science Juris Celmins, Minister of Finance Roberts Zile, Minister of Welfare Vladimir Makarov, Minister of Environment Protection and Regional Development Anatolijs Gorbunovs and State Minister of State Revenues Aija Pocha.

- Foreign Minister Valdis Birkavs and his Finnish counterpart Tarya Karin Halonen signed an agreement on visa-free travel between Latvia and Finland. The agreement will come into force on August 1. On August 4 a similar agreement could be signed with Sweden.
- Latvia's main energy utility Latvenergo has decided not to ask the Council of Energy Supply to increase tariffs for thermal energy next season.
- Three Latvian citizens were murdered in western Ukraine. Two Russian citizens have been charged with the crime.
- One million of the state's shares in Unibanka were auctioned at the Riga stock exchange for 3.22 million lats.
